intro:
Use it for a widget that is a list of rows under a title: deploys, settings, activity, service status. A panel of rows sits in a tray, and the tray's strip along the top carries the title, so the header needs no rule or background of its own.

`band` holds a bordered card in a thin muted band, for a widget that shows one figure or chart rather than a list. `inset` floats the panel in a recessed band and gives `Frame.Footer` a place for actions. `plain` drops the tray, for a frame inside a card or another container that already draws an edge.

It has no state of its own and renders as a server component. A row with `href` is a link and one with `onClick` is a button.

For a single surface with a heading and a body, use [Card](/docs/web/components/card).

parts.Header: The strip above the panel: a title, an optional description, and `Frame.Action` on the trailing side.
parts.Title: A quiet caption in the header. Inside `Frame.Content` it is the row's subject instead: full colour, and cut to one line. Use `as="p"` there.
parts.Description: A line under a title, in the header or in a row.
parts.Action: The header's trailing side: a short status, a link, a small button.
parts.Panel: The card the rows sit on. It draws the hairline between its children.
parts.Row: One line of the panel. `href` makes it a link, `onClick` a button, and `chevron` marks one that leads somewhere.
parts.Media: A row's leading icon or avatar. It keeps its size.
parts.Content: The middle of a row. It takes the space left and can shrink past its content, so a long line truncates instead of pushing the actions off the edge.
parts.Actions: A row's trailing side: a badge, a value, a switch. It keeps its size.
parts.Section: A titled group of rows, for a panel holding more than one.
parts.Footer: The strip below the panel. Under `inset` its children become equal-width pills.

examples.title: Band
examples.description: `variant="band"` holds a bordered card in a thin muted band whose top strip names what is inside. It suits a widget with one thing to show: here a [KPI](/docs/web/components/kpi) and its chart.

examples.title: Inset
examples.description: The panel floats in a recessed band, and the band below it holds the footer's actions as equal pills.

examples.title: Rows that lead somewhere
examples.description: Give a row `href` and it is a link with hover and focus states. `chevron` adds the trailing arrow.

examples.title: Sections
examples.description: `Frame.Section` groups rows under a small heading, and divides its own rows the way the panel does.

examples.title: Inside a card
examples.description: `plain` drops the tray, so a frame inside a card has one edge rather than two. Hold it 8px off the card's edge and give the panel the card's radius less that gap.

notes:
The panel draws a hairline between each of its children, so rows never need to know whether they come first.

Under `band` and `inset` the panel's corners are the shell's less the band, so the two curves stay concentric.

The variant reaches the parts through a data attribute and CSS rather than React context, which is what keeps the frame a server component.
